references.text: The same type of sacrificial animals (bulls, rams, and lambs) is mentioned in connection with other festival offerings, showing the consistent pattern for burnt offerings in the festivals of the Mosaic Law.
Describes the burnt offering on the Feast of Trumpets using similar language about 'a pleasing aroma to the Lord' and requiring unblemished animals.
The second day of the Feast of Tabernacles with a reduced number of bulls (twelve), showing the decreasing progression through the festival.
The concluding day of the Feast of Tabernacles with only one bull, showing the completion of the offering cycle that began with thirteen bulls.
The basic commandment about the Feast of Tabernacles for seven days with fire offerings to the Lord, which Numbers 29:13 expands on with specific offering details.
The burnt offering is described as 'a pleasing aroma, a fire offering to the Lord' - the same terminology is used in Numbers 29:13.
After the exile, the Israelites celebrated the Feast of Tabernacles with daily burnt offerings according to the regulation, which includes this verse.
A prophetic vision that all nations will celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles in the messianic age, showing the enduring significance of the festival.
